candidates.title: Prepare phone game-test logs for Sheets

demandEvidence.chore: I have tried a Schedule Trigger plus Google Drive Watch Files and also a Webhook from a shortcut on the phone, but the workflow either doesn’t fire at all or fires twice on the same file.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I have tried a Schedule Trigger plus Google Drive Watch Files and also a Webhook from a shortcut on the phone, but the workflow either doesn’t fire at all or fires twice on the same file.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable CSV row for each supplied game-test log, with duplicate or incomplete files flagged.
inputs: Synthetic CSV row with timestamp, battery, temperature, frame drops, and test note
Synthetic file name and upload time
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a completed sample log file for a test run.
steps: Read the supplied sample file without accessing a phone or real account.
Check required columns and parse each row into the proposed sheet format.
Compare file name and row fingerprint with a synthetic processed-file list.
Flag duplicate, incomplete, or unparseable rows instead of silently adding them.
Show the proposed rows and exceptions for a person to review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a fixed synthetic file, parsed values must match its rows exactly; a second copy must be flagged and no invalid row may be silently accepted.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies fictional test files, confirms any column mapping, and authorizes any real upload or sheet change.
unverified: Phone shortcut upload behavior and n8n trigger execution are unverified.
Stable duplicate detection across real uploads is unverified.
The post says logging is done for a couple of phones, but wider frequency and buyer demand are unknown.

ease.reason: A beginner can test supplied synthetic CSV files, but no supplied reference supports n8n trigger or Sheets mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent game testers may pay to reduce manual log transfer; this post shows no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic file parser and duplicate flagger is bounded; phone uploads and live sheet writes remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: Parsing and duplicate checks can repeat in a mock, but no execution reference is supplied and a person reviews exceptions.

evidence.reason: The retained task span names trigger failures and duplicate processing; context describes manual phone logs and later CSV transfer, but broader demand is unknown.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a proposed bounded experiment. The mean is below 6; retain as an explicit below-threshold decision.

candidates.title: Test agent recovery from simulated failures

demandEvidence.chore: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

experimentPlan.output: A test report showing whether a supplied agent task can resume safely after a simulated failure without repeating a completed step.
inputs: Synthetic sequence of agent steps and expected outputs
Synthetic checkpoint state before a simulated interruption
Operator-defined rule for which steps are safe to retry
experimentPlan.trigger: A developer supplies a test sequence and selects a simulated interruption point.
steps: Record the expected result and completion state for each synthetic step.
Simulate a stop before and after a selected step.
Compare restart behavior with the supplied checkpoint state.
Flag repeated completed steps and missing recovery state.
Produce a proposed recovery checklist for developer review.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Across a fixed set of synthetic interruptions, the report must identify each deliberately repeated completed step and each missing checkpoint without claiming the agent actually recovered.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A developer defines safe retry rules and reviews all recovery recommendations before changing production behavior.
unverified: No supplied implementation reference documents checkpoint storage, recovery execution, or idempotency.
Production agent behavior, data durability, and safe retry semantics are unverified.
The post establishes developer effort, not a paying customer or frequency.

ease.reason: A developer can test a synthetic interruption table, but no supplied reference supports recovery implementation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: teams building agents may pay for recovery testing; the post establishes developer effort, not buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic test report is feasible, while durable checkpoints and safe production retries remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed analysis can repeat on test cases, but it does not execute recovery and a developer must define safe retries.

evidence.reason: The post explicitly names checkpointing, recovery logic, and idempotency as developer work; frequency and corroboration are absent.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a proposed bounded experiment. The mean is below 6; retain as an explicit below-threshold decision.

candidates.title: Prevent duplicate Shopify lead batches

demandEvidence.chore: Missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewable lead batch with repeated synthetic store records flagged before they are added again.
inputs: Synthetic batch of store identifiers and scoring fields
Operator-supplied batch date and expected input count
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator submits a scheduled lead batch or replays the same sample batch.
steps: Load the supplied synthetic batch and prior processed-store list.
Check that each row has the operator-defined store key and required score fields.
Create a proposed batch key from the supplied date and input identifier.
Compare store keys and the batch key with the synthetic processed list.
Flag repeats and missing fields for review before producing a clean preview.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Submitting an identical sample batch twice must flag the second copy and preserve all distinct stores; missing keys must be reported rather than silently merged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies fictional test rows, chooses the stable store key and scoring rules, and reviews flagged records before any live outreach or system update.
unverified: Actual schedule-trigger behavior and recovery after a missed run are unsupported by supplied implementation evidence.
The source does not establish stable identifiers, production inputs, lead-generation frequency, or paying customers.
Any live Shopify, CRM, or outreach connection would need permission and privacy review.

ease.reason: A beginner can test duplicate suppression with synthetic lead batches, but no supplied reference documents schedule-trigger mechanics.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: Shopify-focused lead-generation consultants may pay for reliable batch processing; the post does not establish buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can compare repeated synthetic batches and flag duplicate records; live Shopify or schedule execution remains unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed batch-key check can repeat on test data, but no implementation reference supports execution and a person reviews exceptions.

evidence.reason: The task span identifies missed schedule triggers duplicating processing in a lead-generation workflow; frequency and buyer demand are unknown.

candidates.reason: Assessed the specifically assigned missed-trigger duplicate-processing chore as a proposed synthetic batch experiment. Its provisional mean is below 6, so it is not proposed for publication.
